highlights.title: Caterpillar is bringing to AI deployment what it learned from automating mining
highlights.summary: Caterpillar has spent decades putting autonomous machines to work at remote mining sites. It's now bringing that experience to AI deployment.
body: Nearly every company that’s trying to deploy artificial intelligence runs into the same problem: it’s hard to integrate the tech into everyday operations. Industrial heavyweight Caterpillar has spent decades dealing with a version of that problem in the physical world, and now it’s using its experience to deploy AI.

Caterpillar’s push into the autonomous space started with mining, where labor shortages and hazardous conditions can make automation particularly useful. Today, it sells automated haul trucks, drilling, underground loaders, dozers, remote-controlled construction equipment, and more. It also offers a software command center, fleet management, and even remote terrain intelligence as part of its autonomous toolkit.

“Now we’re in this super exciting time where we can take all of that learning from mining and bring it into much more dynamic environments, jobsites, quarries, and construction sites,” the company’s CTO, Jaime Mineart, told TechCrunch on the sidelines of the Ai4 conference in Las Vegas earlier this month.

It's now bringing that experience to AI deployment.

highlights.title: The Witcher 4 Will Still Get A Physical Release, Even Though It's Launching In 2028
highlights.summary: CD Projekt has confirmed that a physical version of The Witcher 4 will be released, even though the RPG is slated to launch after Sony stops producing physical games for PlayStation 5.
body: Sony plans to end the production of game discs for PlayStation consoles in January 2028. The Witcher 4 is the highest-profile AAA game currently slated to launch that year, and it comes from a studio that enjoys releasing its games physically. In an interview with The Game Business, CD Projekt joint CEO Michał Nowakowski confirmed that CD Projekt would still like to release a physical version of The Witcher 4.

"We’re big fans of people having access to tangible collectible things. We’re nerds ourselves, and we like that. We always supported that," Nowakowski explained. "So, whatever is the case, we’re going to be for sure having a box. We’re going to have a box that’s going to have some feelies in it. Something you’re going to be wanting to open up and enjoy."

highlights.title: The kindness of strangers: My car had been towed and my kids had no shoes, then a man made a wonderful offer
highlights.summary: Can you help me?, I asked. I think my car’s been towed away, and my children don’t have any shoes. One of the first things we did after moving from the UK to Vancouver was buy a car. Unfortunately, I didn’t acquaint myself with the new road rules quite as quickly.
body: Which is to say, I didn’t know you aren’t allowed to park on busy streets after 3pm in Vancouver. Unaware and in a carefree summer mood, I parked outside an ice-cream shop and took my barefoot children in for a treat. We emerged a short time later, sticky and splattered in drops of raspberry, mint and chocolate, and found my car wasn’t there.

We were so fresh to Canada that we were still staying in a hotel. So I headed out on foot, one kid under each arm, towards our accommodation. When I reached the concierge desk of the valet parking place out the front, I frantically turned to the nicely dressed man standing there and launched into explaining our situation.
“Hi, can you help me? I think my car’s been towed away, and my children don’t have any shoes. I’m sorry about the ice-cream, but can you help me get to wherever the towing place is?”

He answered yes, of course, he was happy to help. After I badgered him about whether he’d have car seats for the kids, he said that we best get going, as he had to be back by 5pm. When I asked why, he replied, “Well, I’ve got a flight to catch.”

highlights.title: Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell are suing Anthropic
highlights.summary: Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell have filed suit against Anthropic in the US District Court for the Northern District of California seeking damages for "tens of thousands" copyrighted works.
body: The companies call it “one of the largest and most blatant ongoing thefts of intellectual property in history.”

This is just the latest high-profile suit against Anthropic, which recently settled a suit brought by the publishing industry for $1.5 billion. It’s also faced multiple lawsuits from Universal Music Group, Concord, and ABKCO, plus separate suits from BMG and Round Hill Music.

In addition to suing Anthropic as an entity, the complaint names Co-Founders Dario Amodei and Benjamin Mann as individual defendants. The suit alleges that Mann used BitTorrent to download over five million pirated books, and that employees downloaded at least two million more from Pirate Library Mirror. It also claims that Anthropic scraped lyrics from sites like MusixMatch and LyricFind, which paid to license content from the labels.

highlights.title: How to make key lime pie | Felicity Cloake's Masterclass
highlights.summary: The indulgent, pleasantly mouth-puckering Floridian dessert in nine easy steps. Beautiful as the Florida Keys are, with average August temperatures topping 30C and with hurricane season looming, I think I’d rather enjoy their most famous culinary export in the calm of our own more temperate isles…
body: In the States, this would involve graham crackers, which are sweeter and more crisp than our digestive biscuits. The latter do make a decent substitute, but feel free to swap in any other biscuits you like the idea of with lime (I suspect ginger nuts would be rather good).

Heat the oven to 180C (160C fan)/350F/gas 4 and lightly grease a 20cm tart tin – not too shallow a one, ideally, and preferably loose-bottomed if you’re planning on taking the pie out of the tin to serve. Crush the biscuits to a fine crumb, either using a food processor or by wrapping them in a clean tea towel and whacking with a rolling pin.

Melt the fat in a microwave or a small saucepan – butter is the classic choice, but I like the flavour of coconut oil here – then stir into the crumbs with a pinch of salt. Tip into the tin, use your hands to press down the mix into an even crust across the base and up the sides, then press down again with the base of a glass.

Bake the crust for about 15 minutes, until it’s dry to the touch, then take out of the oven and leave to cool (though not mandatory, this step will give a crisper crust that holds together much better upon slicing, so it’s worth turning on the oven for).

highlights.title: Musicians-turned-detectives are hunting for AI grifters
highlights.summary: As audio-focused generative tools and platforms have gotten more sophisticated, the internet has become increasingly filled with AI-generated music whose melodies and vocals are algorithmically derived from the work of human artists.
body: As AI infiltrates the electronic dance music scene, a callout culture is brewing.

For musicians — especially those creating art in technologically-focused spaces like electronic dance music — the increasingly complicated question of what is “real” and what isn’t feels particularly urgent and personal. Professional courtesy can make this only more complex; listeners can call out performers they suspect of using gen AI, but it’s something else for artists to raise concerns about their professional peers. There are some though, like 26-year-old EDM producer Max “H4RRIS” Harris, who are taking a stand against generative technology with videos calling out anyone they believe is trying to pass off AI slop as human-made art.

When I recently spoke with Harris, he told me that he sees AI-generated music as “a kind of decoy art form,” and he thinks that the people making it don’t really have anything meaningful to say with their creations. He feels that true art in any medium is “created by people that are trying to express feelings and messages,” and he believes that the only thing AI boosters are really interested in is making a quick profit.

highlights.title: Big business has shown small firms what to do – and what not to do – with AI | Gene Marks
highlights.summary: Small business owners have watched large companies fumble – and sometimes succeed – with AI, and then use what works. One thing I’ve learned about corporate America is that what it succeeds at ultimately trickles down to benefit small businesses.
body: The good news is that it’s also the same for what they fail at.

This is the lesson so far with artificial intelligence. Thanks to the billions invested – and in many cases squandered – by big brands, SMBs (small and mid-sized businesses) have learned what works, what doesn’t, where to spend and where to abstain. Small businesses should be grateful. We’re getting the answers without paying for all the mistakes.

What works: AI for software development, customer service, security and voice. Big technology companies are already using AI to write, review and test code, allowing smaller development teams to accomplish more. Other firms have leaned in to AI to help with a variety of customer service processes with some success. IT departments are relying heavily on AI-enabled security platforms to detect and remedy unusual behavior, phishing attacks, and other vulnerabilities. Big brands are rolling out more AI-powered voice systems that answer incoming calls and perform rudimentary actions.
A countless number of the developers laid off by big tech are using AI tools to replicate themselves and provide services for smaller companies on a larger scale, and we’re hiring them.

highlights.title: CBS's Legendary 82-Episode Sci-Fi Action Series is Officially Free to Watch on Streaming
highlights.summary: Before the release of the movies Blade, X-Men, and Spider-Man, in the late 1990s and early 2000s, it was tough to be a Marvel fan. Outside of the comic books, there were slim pickings of other media that took Marvel characters seriously.
body: Developed by television veteran Kenneth Johnson ( V, The Six Million Dollar Man, The Bionic Woman ), The Incredible Hulk was an hour-long primetime television show aimed at adults. It starred Bill Bixby as Dr. David Banner (I’ll get back to that name later), a scientist who was exposed to gamma radiation in his laboratory. Whenever David loses his temper, he transforms into the Hulk, an enormous, muscle-bound monster.

In the first episode of the series, Banner’s transformation occurs and a fire breaks out at the laboratory. When the Hulk is spotted in the wreckage, he is believed to have killed Banner. This forces Hulk/Banner to go on the run. For the rest of the series, Banner works odd jobs and tries to escape the shadow of the Hulk, which he can never seem to do.

After kicking off with two TV movies in 1977, The Incredible Hulk ran for five seasons, totaling 80 episodes. It ended in 1982, but was then followed up by two TV movies in the late 1980s. Then in 1990, it concluded with The Death of the Incredible Hulk (although Death isn’t on Tubi, for some reason).

highlights.title: “We’re not doing 30 bets a year”: Vijay Pande on betting small after running $4 billion at a16z
highlights.summary: Vijay Pande — who left a16z's roughly $4 billion biotech practice last year to start the much smaller, AI-native VZVC — talks about why biology is finally shifting from a "discovery" science to an "engineering" one, why clinical trials are still brutally expensive, and why he thinks open, shared…
body: It used to be that Vijay Pande was better known in academic circles than investor circles. That changed pretty abruptly a dozen years ago, when Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz — who’d spent their firm’s first five years explicitly avoiding healthcare and life sciences — decided the category was worth betting on after all and handed the keys to Pande. At the time, he was a Stanford chemistry professor who was best known for building Folding@home, the distributed-computing project that turned millions of home PCs into a supercomputer for disease research. Over the next decade-plus, he grew a16z’s bet into a practice managing close to $4 billion.

So it was somewhat unexpected when in June of last year, Pande walked away from it all to start something much smaller. In fact, his new firm, VZVC, co-founded with longtime investor Zach Werner, is built around a handful of concentrated bets a year rather than dozens, it has no associates, and it relies heavily on AI for its day-to-day operations.

A deal for the Brazil international is believed to be at an advanced stage and, while the finer details still require finalising, the transfer is expected to be completed before Tuesday's deadline.
Napoli had shown an interest in Jesus, but the 29-year-old is set to join last season's Spanish league champions and will travel for a medical on Monday.
Jesus joined Arsenal from Manchester City in 2022, scoring 32 goals and adding 22 assists in 123 appearances for the Gunners.

highlights.title: Fable Will Officially Be 20 Hours Long, Xbox Confirms In New Interview
highlights.summary: At Gamescom, Polygon learned just how long it will take players to beat Fable, the upcoming RPG from Playground Games and Xbox Game Studios, when it launches next year.
body: RPGs can range in size and scope, so the question of how long Fable will be came up during a group Q&A attended by Polygon at Gamescom 2026. We learned that it'll take roughly 20 hours to beat the main story. The developers also teased that completing all of Fable's side content and engaging with the previously teased NPC interactions could extend that play time even further.

"We have around 15-20 hours of mainline quest gameplay, we have around 15-20 of side and open-world exploration content gameplay," associate game director Will Kennedy told Polygon. "And then, of course, the life systems are limitless, so you can play them for as long as you want."

Someone else in the group Q&A said that Fable is "not a huge game" in response to Kennedy's answer, which caused another associate game director from Playground Games, Craig Littler, to chime in. "As Will just said, you can literally play it forever if that's what you want to do," Littler reiterated.

highlights.title: Italy may ban staring at your phone while crossing the street. Why stop there? | Dave Schilling
highlights.summary: The move sends the right signal. While we’re at it, can we ban using ringtones and scooting on the sidewalk? Imagine driving in Italy, with its narrow, cobblestone streets and scooter enthusiasts.
body: The modern world is just too hectic for the ancient streets of Europe, so Italy is considering doing the only sensible thing it can: outlawing texting in crosswalks. The Italian government’s updated draft of its highway code proposes fines of €75 or more for anyone caught sending a DM, updating their LinkedIn, finishing Wordle on the fifth guess, or anything else phone-related that might make them miss an oncoming metal projectile. I’m sure most people will risk the slap on wrist to get that message off, but it at least sends a signal to the Italian people that paying attention to traffic is actually kind of important.

highlights.summary: Plus: Hackers target over 100 US water systems, ICE puts in an order for robot dogs, and you’ll never guess what “MrChildPorn” was arrested for.
body: You may have noticed that Flock Safety’s automatic license plate reader cameras—and the cops who misuse them—are getting a lot of coverage lately. This week, WIRED found a particularly wild case: A cop in Alpharetta, Georgia, was accused of searching for the license plate of a coworker dozens of times after an affair between the two ended, according to internal documents obtained by WIRED.

The same police department where the former lovers worked also shared the data captured from its Flock cameras with more than 2,000 police departments, colleges, and other organizations across the United States, and accessed data from more than 1,300 entities in exchange.
Also at the intersection of love and surveillance, background-check company PeopleFinder is making use of its extensive dossiers on people to start a new dating site called Stud or Dud.

highlights.title: The datacenter fight could permanently transform US politics. Which party will seize advantage?
highlights.summary: The movement against datacenters are uniting Americans because they perfectly illustrate how a few individuals hold all the power to control decisions that impact our lives. Bryce Gustafson has been knocking on doors in Indiana for more than a decade.
body: Gustafson said he’s had similar conversations all across the state. If there’s one thing he sees uniting Hoosiers of all stripes – from rural areas such as Morgan county to suburbs such as Franklin Township to the historically African American neighborhood of Martindale-Brightwood in Indianapolis – it’s fury over these water-guzzling, air-polluting behemoths and the tech oligarchs imposing them.

Today, three-quarters of Americans oppose local datacenter development, a swing of more than 30 points in just a year. More than 500 counties and municipalities have passed datacenter bans or moratoria, while dozens of proposed projects have been killed outright. And the issue has come to define some of the highest-profile political races in the country. In the battle for US Senate in Ohio, populist Democrat Sherrod Brown has made Republican senator Jon Husted’s support of datacenters the centerpiece of his campaign, prompting warnings from the National Republican senatorial committee that “datacenters are the anchor hanging around Husted’s neck”.

highlights.title: Phasmophobia's second Quality of Life update adds Restricted maps, VR fixes, and much creepier deaths
highlights.summary: Kinetic Games has released Phasmophobia 's second Quality of Life update, adding a raft of new Restricted maps, streamlined Evidence collection, VR fixes, and considerably more ways to die.
body: Now live on PC and PlayStation (the Xbox release is "to follow"), the Quality of Life Part 2 update builds on Quality of Life Part 1 which introduced the revamped 13 Willow Street map back in July alongside a batch of other gameplay tweaks.

We're getting a (long-overdue!) set of new small-to-medium Restricted maps for Prison, Brownstone High School, and Point Hope, bringing condensed versions of the original maps designed to speed up investigations and add more variety to runs.

Evidence collection has also been streamlined. Rather than manually checking the in-game journal, players can now tell whether a piece of evidence has already been logged directly from their Photo Camera, Video Camera, or Sound Recorder via faded overlays and yellow LEDs.
Evidence and ghost types selected by teammates will also now show up for the whole team, cutting down on last-minute double-checking before a hunt.

highlights.title: ’17’ Review: Harrowing Teen Pregnancy Drama from Macedonia Could Be the Feel-Bad Movie of the Year
highlights.summary: From the first frame, Kosara Mitić’s “17” refuses to pull any punches, plunging us immediately into the traumatic moment when a hookup between high-school student Sara (Eva Kostić) and two boys takes a violent turn.
body: Sarajevo Best Actress winner Eva Kostić captivates in this unflinching portrait of peer pressure and sexual shame by first time writer-director Kosara Mitić.

When the group arrives by bus, Sara is a conspicuously surly presence in her baggy sweatshirt and dragging jeans; her classmates, brusque, yappy, and shockingly entitled as they constantly talk back to their two teacher-chaperones, both grossly resigned to their students’ insolence. Denied the private room she paid double for because of a mix-up by hotel management, Sara must room with her guileless, overly eager friend Lina (Martina Danilovska) and her cool-girl ex bestie Nina (Eva Stojcevska). Nina is now dating the apish Filip (Dame Joveski), Sara’s ex and one of her rapists — unbeknownst to everyone, of course.

highlights.title: Chess.com launched a poker site and is planning even more classic games
highlights.summary: Chess.com has done one thing, and one thing very well, for almost 20 years, but now it's going beyond its domain name. The biggest name in online chess quietly launched its first companion site in beta back in May: Gambit, a free online poker website where players can learn the game without risking…
body: Chess.com’s Albert Cheng says AI helped get Gambit off the ground with just a two-person team.

Chess.com’s chief growth officer, Albert Cheng, told The Verge the company chose poker for its first companion site because, like chess, it has learning and social elements on top of just playing the game. He also promised there will never be real-money gambling on Gambit, saying, “Real money is the problem we built Gambit to get away from, the whole industry makes money when beginners lose. We’d rather build a place where people can actually learn.”

Gambit will look familiar to anyone who’s used Chess.com. It borrows the same design style and includes similar play modes, like bot matches, games with friends, tournaments, a review mode for studying your past games, and a learning mode. Gambit even includes Chess.com’s bot characters, with matching skill levels — I immediately recognized “Martin,” the lowest skill level bot from Chess.com, who is also the lowest skill level bot on Gambit.

highlights.title: How to Run a Chatbot on Your Own Computer
highlights.summary: Installing a large language model on your personal computer gives you a handy digital assistant that won’t compromise your data privacy.
body: It's no exaggeration to say the large language models that power AI bots like ChatGPT and Gemini are changing the world. Many of us are now relying on them for coding, writing, summarizing, and searching the web. Whatever directions AI goes in over the next few years, LLMs will be part of that future.

If you use ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, or any of the other AI platforms, then you're using an LLM. What's less commonly known is that these LLMs can be run locally, on your own computer. The key benefits are offline access and greater privacy, because you're not sending anything to the cloud for anyone else to analyze or review.

You're also not paying any AI companies a monthly subscription or hitting any usage rates. Numerous LLMs are available to download for free, including from big names like Meta and Google. Though they tend not to be as advanced or as speedy as the LLMs inside the apps you have to pay for, they're capable enough for everyday use, and you can pick and choose between them as needed.

highlights.title: PSA: Nintendo Switch 2 Gets a $50 Price Increase on Tuesday
highlights.summary: Compared to Sony and Microsoft, Nintendo has done an admirable job of keeping the price of the Switch 2 reasonably low amid rising component prices. But not even Mario is immune to market forces, and Nintendo is raising the Switch 2’s price by $50 on September 1.
body: When it comes to buying a Switch 2, you used to have more options than you do today. Previously, you could buy the console all by itself, or bundled with a game. There was even a bundle that let you choose among three first-party games. As we creep toward the price hike, however, all of the bundles have vanished from retailers. Your only reasonably priced option now is wither to buy a Switch 2 new or refurbished.

New Switch 2 consoles are available at all the usual retailers ( see at Amazon ). Refurbished Switch 2s are available at several retailers, but the best deal going right now is a “Grade A” refurbished unit at Woot for $399.99. That’s $50 less than the current price of a new Switch 2, and it’s the best deal going if you don’t mind refurbished hardware.
Woot, by the way, is owned by Amazon, so you can rest assured it’s a legit retailer. I’ve bought many things from Woot and never had any problems.

highlights.title: 10 Best '70s Movies That Could Never Be Made Today
highlights.summary: Plenty of films in the 1970s challenged audiences with provocative material, and even though these movies are revered now, they'd never be made today.
body: Here are 10 movies from the 1970s that couldn't be made today.

"Deliverance" features the kind of pensive, shocking, and dark subject matter that major studios don't pursue as heavily today, and its production was dangerous as all get out. The story of four civilized men from the city who seek to canoe down the rapids of a soon-to-be-dammed river and come face-to-face with the random violence and savagery of the natural world was shot on location in Rabun County, Georgia, and you can feel the real-life peril of the actors performing dangerous in-camera stunts.

Warner Bros. was already nervous about the John Boorman-directed film's thematic content during production, and they slashed the budget. That led the main performers to do it themselves: Jon Voight got shots of him actually free-climbing the cliffside, Burt Reynolds wanted a go at being in one of the canoes as it went over a waterfall, and Ned Beatty nearly drowned while shooting other footage of the rapids. A huge fistfight also broke out on set, though that was more of an occupational hazard related to stubborn creatives than dying at the hands of nature.

highlights.summary: On Saturday, the beauty founder and musician tied the knot in Santa Barbara—but only after the bride invited Vogue along to the final fitting of her four Oscar de la Renta wedding looks in Beverly Hills.
body: Congratulations are in order for Finneas and Claudia Sulewski: the couple married on Saturday, August 29, in Montecito, surrounded by family and friends. Just under two weeks before, Vogue followed along as the actor and beauty founder bride headed to the Oscar de la Renta boutique in Beverly Hills for the final fitting of her four wedding weekend looks, all custom-made by the legendary American fashion house. “I’m so excited,” Claudia says, inviting us through the door. “Let’s go!”

The morning began with Claudia greeting her mom, Beata Sulewska, and her now-mother-in-law, Maggie Baird, and outlining the run of show: trying on her rehearsal dinner dress, ceremony dress, first dance and reception dress, and the after-party dress. The one she’s most excited about? The main ceremony dress, of course. “Every fitting thus far has sort of been an alteration, so I’m really excited to try on the final version,” Claudia adds.
Claudia in her after-party dress, accompanied by (from left to right) friends Dru MacDonald and Rebecca Black, her mother Beata Krupinska-Sulewski, and her now-mother-in-law Maggie Baird.
